newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Gov. proposes $36 bln biennial budget.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Gov. proposes $36 bln biennial budget.

text.p: The administration of Ohio Gov. George Voinovich proposed a $36.14 billion fiscal 1998-99 biennial general fund budget that would boost spending on schools.

The budget, which was unveiled in Columbus by state budget director Greg Browning, would increase spending on primary and secondary schools to $4.1 billion or 4 percent in fiscal 1998 and to $4.3 billion or 4.9 percent in fiscal 1999.

In his state of the state address last month, Voinovich called education the state's "number one priority" and outlined plans to reduce funding inequities among school districts, hike the level of annual per-pupil state funding, and spend money on school buildings.
Overall, the governor's spending plan calls for a $17.6 billion general fund budget in fiscal 1998, which begins July 1, and an $18.5 billion budget in the second year of the bienium.

According to an overview from the state budget office, the proposed budget calls for no state tax increases, continuation of an income tax reduction passed last year by lawmakers, and maintenance of an adequate budget stabilization fund.
That fund currently stands at nearly five percent of annual state revenues, the overview said.

The proposed budget projects a $157 million unreserved ending balance for fiscal 1997, which ends June 30, and unreserved balances of $212.5 million at the end of fiscal 1998 and $91 million at the end of fiscal 1999.
